verdict.rationale: Galileo is an AI evaluation and observability platform, and user-configured background automations are a fair axis for it. The closest evidence is threshold-based alerts on logs, which watch metrics over a time window and notify users. That is a related monitoring and notification feature, not documented user-defined automations or workflows that run and act autonomously, so it earns no credit here. The evidence pack documents no scheduled jobs, recurring experiment runs, or trigger-action automations.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background
